_about: Welcome card and guided tours. The same file is in both apps: apps/web/src/tours/tours.json in the web repo and src/ui/tours/tours.json in the desktop repo. Keep the two identical; each app's tests check its copy. A step with "apps" shows only in those apps ("web", "desktop").

welcome.title: Welcome to Collaborative Brick Layout Designer
welcome.text: Plan a LEGO layout for your next show, on your own or with your club.

layout.label: Start or open a layout
layout.text: Begin with an empty map, or open a file from this app or BlueBrick.

club.label: Join a club
club.text: Share layouts, venues and parts with the people you build with.

tour.label: Take the tour
tour.text: A few short steps that show you the main buttons.

steps.title: All your pieces live here
steps.text: Search by name, or pick a group like Track or Baseplate. Drag a piece onto the map to place it.

steps.title: Sheets
steps.text: A layout is built on sheets, like see-through pages. Hide one to see what is under it.

steps.title: Place and move
steps.text: Click a piece to pick it, then drag it to move it. Drag a box around pieces to pick several.

steps.title: Bend flexible track
steps.text: Pick a flexible track, then drag the round handle at its free end to bend it.

steps.title: Saving and live sync
steps.text: This shows whether your changes are saved. In a shared layout, everyone's changes appear live.

steps.title: Share a picture
steps.text: Make a picture of your layout to post, print or send to your club.

steps.title: Help is always here
steps.text: Click a ? for a quick tip. The Help menu has the other tours and all help topics.

steps.title: Draw your venue
steps.text: Draw the walls first, then add doors, openings and things in the way, like pillars.

steps.title: Real sizes
steps.text: Type sizes in feet and inches or meters. The app works out the studs for you.

steps.title: Straight walls
steps.text: Snap keeps walls straight and corners square while you draw.

steps.title: Trace a floor plan
steps.text: Have a plan of the hall? Put the picture underneath and draw over it.

steps.title: Save the venue
steps.text: Save it, and start new layouts from it whenever you show there.

steps.title: Your server
steps.text: This shows whether you are connected to your club's server. Click it to add a server or sign in.

steps.title: Everything on your server
steps.text: Open from Server shows your layouts, venues, modules and parts, and your clubs', in one place.

steps.title: Mine and my clubs'
steps.text: Pick All, Mine or a club to see just those layouts, venues and parts.

steps.title: Save to
steps.text: When you make or publish a layout, Save to picks whether it is yours or your club's.

steps.title: Modules shared with you
steps.text: Share a module with your club from its ⋯ menu. Ones shared with you are in Shared with me, with their owner's updates.

steps.title: Partner clubs
steps.text: Partner clubs share modules both ways, with no accept each time. Admins and Managers ask and answer on the club's page.

steps.title: Partner clubs
steps.text: Partner requests and offers wait on the Modules tab and in your notifications. Answer them there with Accept or Decline.

steps.title: Your notifications
steps.text: Requests to join, invites and news from your clubs land here. Answer them with Accept or Decline, right from the list.

steps.title: Your club's page
steps.text: The club page shows who is in the club. Admins invite people from there.

steps.title: Joining a club
steps.text: A club admin sends you an invite link. Open it to join, and the club's things show up here.

steps.title: Modules
steps.text: A module is parts that move as one piece, like a table a club member brings. This layout's modules are listed here.

steps.title: Make a module
steps.text: Pick some parts, then Make a module. Save it to your Module library to use it again in other layouts.

steps.title: Each module's menu
steps.text: The ⋯ menu edits, colors and saves a module. Table and power says what it stands on and the power it needs.

steps.title: Tables and power
steps.text: The layout adds up its modules' outlets, watts and table heights here, for whoever plans the show.

steps.title: Your routes
steps.text: Routes are named ways along the track. Open this list from Panels; the eye hides one on your map only.

steps.title: Draw a route
steps.text: Press New route, then click on the track where it starts and where it ends. The shortest way is found for you.

steps.title: Stops on the way
steps.text: Shift-click adds a stop, to send the route along another line. Name it and press Save route.

steps.title: Switches follow the route
steps.text: Set switches turns every switch on the route its way. Run mode lets you flip them by hand.

steps.title: Where cars go
steps.text: Places are the industries, yards, staging and interchanges along your track. Open this list from Panels.

steps.title: Name a place
steps.text: Press New place, then click the track where the cars stand. Give it a name and kind, and the cars it takes and sends.

steps.title: Spots
steps.text: A place can have several spots. Each says how many cars fit, worked out from the track unless you type it.

steps.title: On the map
steps.text: View › Places shows each spot and how many cars it holds. Places on a module’s track go along with the module.

steps.title: Cars on the track
steps.text: Drag a car along the track to move it or uncouple it; one that meets another couples. Click a car for its load.

steps.title: Where each car goes
steps.text: Open Live Ops from Panels. Make waybills gives every car somewhere to go, and you can change any of them.

steps.title: Jobs and switch lists
steps.text: A job is one crew's work: the places it stops at. Its switch list says what to set out and pick up.

steps.title: Trains and cars
steps.text: Open Trains from Panels. Rolling stock holds this layout's engines and cars; Trains holds the trains made of them.

steps.title: A quick car, or your own model
steps.text: New car needs just a number and a length. Import a model… makes one of a model you built, wheels and all.

steps.title: Make a train
steps.text: Tick a few cars and press Make a train, or press New train and add them in order, front first.

steps.title: On the track
steps.text: Press Put on the track, then click where its front goes. Each car sits between its trucks, as on real track.

steps.title: Watch it run
steps.text: Press Run, then Play. Each train runs its route at its scale speed; two that would collide both stop.

steps.title: Checks
steps.text: Checks lists what doesn't fit: a train too long for its track, a curve too tight. Show me finds the spot.

steps.title: Your roster
steps.text: Save a car to your roster or a club's to use it in other layouts. Update brings a layout's copy up to date.

steps.title: Look around
steps.text: Drag with one finger to move around. Pinch to zoom in and out.

steps.title: Make changes
steps.text: Tap Edit to change the layout, if you are allowed to. Tap a piece to pick it, then drag it to move it.

steps.title: Saved views
steps.text: Tap the layout's name to jump to a saved view, or to see the whole layout.

steps.title: Share a picture
steps.text: Make a picture of the layout to send to friends.

steps.title: Help is always here
steps.text: Tap ? for tips, and to take the other tours.

steps.title: The desktop app’s importer
steps.text: Your browser reads your model as the desktop app does; if it can’t, the server reads it and deletes it straight after.

steps.title: Line it up
steps.text: Turn the model and move it until its studs sit on the grid.

steps.title: Snap points
steps.text: Uncheck any connection point you don’t want on the part.

steps.title: Where it goes
steps.text: Put it in the layout you have open, or start a new layout with it.

steps.title: Every version is here
steps.text: A version is kept as you work, and before big changes. Pick one to look at it.

steps.title: Keep one now
steps.text: Keep the layout as it is, with a name like Before the show, so you can find it again.

steps.title: Put one back
steps.text: Restore makes the layout as it was. How it is now is kept first, so you can go back.

steps.title: Copy one out
steps.text: Make a new layout from a version, and leave this one as it is.
